part1.q:
Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 1 to 8.
Experiential learning is an educational approach where students learn by engaging in direct experiences. This hands-on method is known for its ability to enhance the learning process by allowing students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world situations. One of the primary benefits of experiential learning is that it fosters deeper understanding and retention of information. By actively participating in the learning process, students are more likely to remember and understand the material. Studies indicate that teenagers who participate in experiential learning programs show a 25% increase in long-term information retention compared to those relying solely on traditional methods.
Moreover, experiential learning encourages critical thinking and problem-solving skills. When students are placed in real-life scenarios, they must navigate challenges and make decisions, which helps develop these crucial skills. This approach also promotes student engagement and motivation, as learners find the material more relevant and interesting when they can see its practical applications.
However, experiential learning is not without its disadvantages. One significant drawback is the potential for unequal access to resources. Not all students may have the same opportunities for hands-on experiences, which can lead to disparities in learning outcomes. Additionally, experiential learning can be time-consuming and may require significant resources, including materials, time, and instructor guidance, which may not always be available.
Despite these challenges, many educators believe that the benefits of experiential learning outweigh the drawbacks. By providing students with the opportunity to apply their knowledge in practical settings, experiential learning prepares them for real-world challenges and enhances their overall educational experience. As educational paradigms continue to evolve, experiential learning remains a valuable tool in the educator's toolkit, particularly as it addresses the unique needs of different age groups, from fostering curiosity in teenagers to improving workplace readiness in adults.
The word fosters in paragraph 1 is OPPOSITE in meaning to _____.

Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 20 to 29.
Chandigarh, a city located in northern India, stands as a striking example of the power of modern urban planning and creative architecture. [I] It was designed in the 1950s by the famous Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier as a symbol of India's progress after independence. [II] The city is carefully planned with a grid-like layout, divided into sectors. [III] This design was made to encourage a sense of community and make daily life convenient. [IV]
Le Corbusier wanted Chandigarh to combine urban living with nature. He included many open spaces, gardens, and green areas in the city's design, earning it the nickname "The City Beautiful." The buildings are modernist in style, using simple geometric shapes and raw concrete materials. The Capitol Complex, an important UNESCO World Heritage Site, is home to the High Court, Secretariat, and Legislative Assembly. These buildings are considered landmarks of architectural innovation.
Chandigarh is also known for its cleanliness and greenery, making it one of the cleanest cities in India. It has many attractions, such as Sukhna Lake, a popular spot for boating and enjoying scenic views, especially at sunset. The Rock Garden, created by Nek Chand using industrial waste and discarded materials, is another must-visit site. This unique sculpture garden has become a heritage site and a favourite destination for families. Other notable places include the Zakir Rose Garden, which hosts the annual Rose Festival, and the Pinjore Gardens, known for their Mughal-style landscaping.
While Chandigarh's design is famous, it has faced some problems. Critics say the strict grid structure makes it hard for the city to grow in a natural way. Its focus on car-centric infrastructure has also led to traffic problems and concerns about the environment. Le Corbusier's idea of building "towers in parks" for housing did not work as planned and had to be changed to fit local needs.
Despite these challenges, Chandigarh is still an important model for urban planning. It shows how good design can balance function and beauty. Cities around the world look to Chandigarh for lessons in creating thoughtful and sustainable urban spaces.
Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 1?
options: Chandigarh in northern India is known for its striking and creative modern urban architectural influence.
Chandigarh in northern India strongly demonstrates the success of contemporary city design and innovative building styles.
Modern urban planning and creative buildings are evident in northern India, especially in Chandigarh.
Chandigarh's modern designs make it stand out as a compelling and creative city in the northern India.

Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 20 to 29.
Chandigarh, a city located in northern India, stands as a striking example of the power of modern urban planning and creative architecture. [I] It was designed in the 1950s by the famous Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier as a symbol of India's progress after independence. [II] The city is carefully planned with a grid-like layout, divided into sectors. [III] This design was made to encourage a sense of community and make daily life convenient. [IV]
Le Corbusier wanted Chandigarh to combine urban living with nature. He included many open spaces, gardens, and green areas in the city's design, earning it the nickname "The City Beautiful." The buildings are modernist in style, using simple geometric shapes and raw concrete materials. The Capitol Complex, an important UNESCO World Heritage Site, is home to the High Court, Secretariat, and Legislative Assembly. These buildings are considered landmarks of architectural innovation.
Chandigarh is also known for its cleanliness and greenery, making it one of the cleanest cities in India. It has many attractions, such as Sukhna Lake, a popular spot for boating and enjoying scenic views, especially at sunset. The Rock Garden, created by Nek Chand using industrial waste and discarded materials, is another must-visit site. This unique sculpture garden has become a heritage site and a favourite destination for families. Other notable places include the Zakir Rose Garden, which hosts the annual Rose Festival, and the Pinjore Gardens, known for their Mughal-style landscaping.
While Chandigarh's design is famous, it has faced some problems. Critics say the strict grid structure makes it hard for the city to grow in a natural way. Its focus on car-centric infrastructure has also led to traffic problems and concerns about the environment. Le Corbusier's idea of building "towers in parks" for housing did not work as planned and had to be changed to fit local needs.
Despite these challenges, Chandigarh is still an important model for urban planning. It shows how good design can balance function and beauty. Cities around the world look to Chandigarh for lessons in creating thoughtful and sustainable urban spaces.
Which of the following is TRUE about the Capitol Complex in Chandigarh?
options: It is a modern housing development that solves urban living challenges.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and includes key government buildings.
It is a traditional Indian architectural site built by concrete materials.
It represents Chandigarh's architectural and environmental challenges.
